# apicp_mail_client_config (Resource)

Publishes mail-client autoconfiguration for an `apicp_mail_domain`, so Thunderbird, Outlook and other clients find the right server settings from just an address: SRV, MX, SPF and DMARC records (created in the account's own `apicp_dns_zone` for the domain when apicp hosts one) and the Thunderbird and Outlook autoconfig documents on the node. Requires `apicp_mail_tls` to be enabled first (apicp refuses otherwise, since the advertised ports only exist with TLS) - use `depends_on`. Records that already exist are left alone, and destroying this resource removes only the records apicp created. Where there is no matching zone, add the `records` marked `manual` with your own DNS provider.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "apicp_mail_tls" "this" {}

resource "apicp_mail_domain" "example" {
  name = "example.com"
}

resource "apicp_mail_client_config" "example" {
  mail_domain_id = apicp_mail_domain.example.id

  # apicp refuses client config until mail TLS is on.
  depends_on = [apicp_mail_tls.this]
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `mail_domain_id` (String) ID of the `apicp_mail_domain`. Changing this replaces the resource.

### Read-Only

- `autoconfig_url` (String) Where clients fetch the Thunderbird autoconfig document.
- `host` (String) Mail server hostname the records point clients at.
- `id` (String) The ID of this resource.
- `records` (Attributes List) The discovery records and what apicp did with each: `created` (apicp published it), `exists` (something was already there, left alone) or `manual` (apicp hosts no matching zone - add it yourself). (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--records))

<a id="nestedatt--records"></a>
### Nested Schema for `records`

Read-Only:

- `action` (String)
- `content` (String)
- `name` (String) Record name relative to the domain (`@` = apex).
- `type` (String)

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
terraform import apicp_mail_client_config.example mdom_abc123
```
